Insight1.summary: In aged female and male mice, senescence and DAM gene expression was more pronounced in fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum white matter than in hippocampal gray matter. Age-dependent increases in these transcriptional signatures were observed more consistently in white matter than in the hippocampus or cerebellum, emphasizing white matter susceptibility to late-life senescence and DAM changes.
Insight1.how: The authors compared RT-PCR measurements from microdissected fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum white matter with hippocampal gray matter in aged female and male mice. Several senescence and DAM-related genes were significantly higher in white matter, with additional female- or male-specific changes among particular transcripts. Comparisons with young, sex-matched mice showed that some genes increased in both gray and white matter, whereas a broader set increased in aged white matter, and the regional heat map showed more consistent age-related increases in white matter than in hippocampus or cerebellum. These findings support regional susceptibility of white matter to late-life transcriptional changes, but do not by themselves establish a mechanistically selective vulnerability.
Insight1.relevant: We investigated senescence and microglial gene expression patterns in microdissected fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum white matter relative to hippocampal gray matter of aged female and male mice (Fig. 1). p16ink4a (Fig. 1a), Cdkn2a (Fig. 1b), Lgals3 (Fig. 1c), Cdkn1a/p21 (Fig. 1d) and Ccl2 (Fig. 1e) expression were significantly higher in fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum compared with hippocampus. In aged female mice, Ccl5 (Fig. 1f), Apoe (Fig. 1g) and Gpr34 (Fig. 1h) expression were significantly higher in fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum compared with hippocampus. Relative to young counterparts, p16ink4a, Cdkn2a, Csf1r, Gpr34 and Trem2 expression increased in both gray and white matter microdissections of old male and female mice (Fig. 1i,j). Apoe, Bcl2a1a, Cd11b, Klk8, Lgals3, Cdkn1a/p21 and Tmem173 expression increased in old female and male fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum. Ccl2, Ccl5, Il1b and Tyrobp increased in old male fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum (Fig. 1j). In aged female and male mice, senescence and DAM gene expression was more pronounced in white matter relative to hippocampal gray matter. At the regional level, we observed age-dependent increases in genes such as p16ink4a, Cdkn2a, Lgals3, Apoe, Bcl2a1a, Cd11b, Csf1r, Klk8, Tmem173, Trem2 and Tyrobp more consistently in old fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum (Fig. 1k) than in the hippocampus or cerebellum, emphasizing that white matter is susceptible to late-life changes in senescence and DAM transcriptional signatures.

Insight2.summary: GAL3+ cells are rare in young mouse brains but accumulate densely in aged white matter tracts, especially the fimbria, where GAL3 colocalizes with IBA1 rather than GFAP. In aged female fimbria, IBA1+GAL3+ cells are larger than IBA1+GAL3− cells and show higher or trending-higher levels of uPAR and CD38; the age-associated increase in GAL3 area is more pronounced in females, while dPP4 elevation was demonstrated only for fimbria myeloid cells overall.
Insight2.how: Immunofluorescence mapped GAL3 in young and aged brains and used IBA1 and GFAP costaining to establish its association with myeloid rather than astrocytic cells in the fimbria. Sex-stratified measurements showed greater GAL3-positive area in old versus young female fimbria, whereas the corresponding male comparison was not significant. Morphological analysis found that IBA1+GAL3+ cells were larger than IBA1+GAL3− cells in old female fimbria, and PCA distinguished populations associated with GAL3 immunoreactivity. Imaging mass cytometry further showed that aged fimbria myeloid cells had greater GAL3, CD38, uPAR, dPP4, IBA1, and CD45 intensity than hippocampal myeloid cells, while the GAL3-stratified analysis specifically supported enrichment of uPAR and CD38, not dPP4.
Insight2.relevant: GAL3+ cells were rare in young mouse brains. In aged brains, we observed GAL3+ cells in multiple limbic regions (Extended Data Fig. 1a) with dense localization in white matter tracts, especially the fimbria (Extended Data Fig. 1a). In aged fimbria, GAL3 signal colocalized with the myeloid/microglial marker IBA1 but not with the astrocyte marker GFAP (Extended Data Fig. 1b,c). GAL3 immunoreactivity comprised a larger area of old versus young female fimbria; however, GAL3 area was not significantly different in fimbria between old and young male mice (Extended Data Fig. 1d). In the old female fimbria, IBA1+GAL3+ cells were larger relative to IBA1+GAL3− cells (Extended Data Fig. 1e,f). PCA of IBA1+GAL3+ and IBA1+GAL3− populations from old mouse fimbria revealed size-specific principal components based on cellular morphology and distinguished by GAL3+ immunoreactivity (Extended Data Fig. 1g). Thus, immunofluorescent imaging and gene expression demonstrate increased abundance of the senescent and DAM marker GAL3/Lgals3 in aged white matter, including the fimbria, which was more pronounced in aged female mice. […] Fimbria myeloid cells exhibited greater intensity of IBA1, GAL3, CD38, uPAR, dPP4 and CD45, relative to hippocampal myeloid cells, which exhibited greater CX3CR1 protein levels (Fig. 2b). Stratification of GAL3+ and GAL3− cells in the fimbria showed that GAL3+ cells harbored trending or significantly higher levels of senescence-related markers uPAR and CD38 (Fig. 2c).

mcq_questions.question: In young mice, GAL3+ cells are rare throughout the brain, but in aged brains they appear in several limbic regions and accumulate densely in white matter tracts, especially the fimbria, where GAL3 colocalizes with IBA1 and not with GFAP. Which conclusion is best supported by this pattern of colocalization?

options.A: GAL3 is expressed by astrocytes in the fimbria because GFAP marks astrocytes and GFAP signal overlaps with GAL3 in aged fimbria. because astrocyte identity is defined by GFAP and the fimbria contains many GFAP+ processes.
options.C: GAL3 in the aged fimbria is associated with a myeloid/microglial population rather than with astrocytes, because GAL3 colocalizes with the myeloid marker IBA1 and does not colocalize with the astrocyte marker GFAP. because colocalization with IBA1 alone, in the absence of GFAP overlap, places GAL3 in IBA1+ cells.
options.B: GAL3 marks neurons in the aged fimbria, because neurons are the dominant cell type in white matter tracts and GAL3 signal is dense there. because dense immunoreactivity in a tract implies the most abundant resident cell type carries the marker.
options.D: GAL3 is restricted to oligodendrocytes in the aged fimbria, because the fimbria is a myelinated tract and GFAP (an astrocyte marker) does not colocalize with GAL3, ruling out any glial source. because non-colocalization with GFAP eliminates astrocytes as the only possible glial carrier.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The stem states that in aged fimbria, GAL3 colocalizes with the myeloid/microglial marker IBA1 but not with the astrocyte marker GFAP. The correct conclusion is therefore that GAL3 in the aged fimbria is associated with a myeloid/microglial population rather than with astrocytes. The reasoning chain is: GAL3+IBA1+ overlap + absence of GAL3+GFAP+ overlap → GAL3 is carried by IBA1+ cells (myeloid), not GFAP+ cells (astrocytes).

distractor_analysis.A: The conclusion (GAL3 is astrocytic) is wrong because the stem explicitly states GAL3 does NOT colocalize with GFAP. The reasoning tries to rescue it by appealing to GFAP as the astrocyte marker, but that is exactly the premise that contradicts the conclusion.
distractor_analysis.B: The conclusion (GAL3 is neuronal) is wrong; the stem does not address neurons, and 'dense in a tract' does not imply the dominant cell type carries the marker. The reasoning conflates abundance of a marker with abundance of the carrier cell type.
distractor_analysis.D: The conclusion (GAL3 is restricted to oligodendrocytes) is wrong and overreaches. Non-colocalization with GFAP rules out astrocytes as the GAL3 carrier, but does not by itself identify oligodendrocytes; the stem provides positive evidence only for IBA1 (myeloid) colocalization.

mcq_questions.question: In aged female fimbria, IBA1+GAL3+ cells are larger than IBA1+GAL3− cells, and PCA of these two populations separates them along size-related components. Imaging mass cytometry shows fimbria myeloid cells have greater GAL3, CD38, uPAR, dPP4, IBA1, and CD45 intensity than hippocampal myeloid cells, and stratification of fimbria myeloid cells by GAL3 shows trending or significantly higher uPAR and CD38 in the GAL3+ subset but does not show the same for dPP4. If one were to conclude that GAL3 expression in aged fimbria myeloid cells marks a senescent-like state with co-upregulation of the senescence-associated markers uPAR and CD38, would this conclusion follow?

options.D: Yes, because GAL3+ cells specifically show trending or significantly higher uPAR and CD38 within the fimbria myeloid population, even though dPP4 elevation was detected only when comparing fimbria vs. hippocampus myeloid cells overall. because the within-fimbria GAL3-stratified analysis is the appropriate test for marker co-expression in the same population.
options.A: Yes, because every marker measured (GAL3, CD38, uPAR, dPP4, IBA1, CD45) is elevated in fimbria versus hippocampal myeloid cells, so all of them must co-vary with GAL3 within the fimbria. because a between-region increase in every marker implies a within-population co-upregulation with GAL3.
options.B: No, because the GAL3-stratified comparison within the fimbria does not show elevated dPP4 in GAL3+ cells, so any claim that GAL3 marks a uniformly senescent-like state with all listed markers would overreach the within-region evidence. because within-population stratification, not between-region differences, tests co-expression with GAL3.
options.C: No, because IBA1+GAL3+ cells being larger than IBA1+GAL3− cells shows that GAL3 marks a morphologically distinct subset but says nothing about senescence marker co-expression. because size differences and marker co-regulation are unrelated measurements.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The stem specifies two distinct comparisons: (1) fimbria vs. hippocampus myeloid cells overall, where GAL3, CD38, uPAR, dPP4, IBA1, and CD45 are all higher in fimbria; and (2) within fimbria myeloid cells stratified by GAL3, where GAL3+ cells show trending or significantly higher uPAR and CD38 but dPP4 is not reported as elevated in the GAL3+ subset. The correct conclusion is that GAL3 expression in aged fimbria myeloid cells does mark a subset with elevated uPAR and CD38 (senescence-associated markers), because the appropriate test for co-expression within the same population is the within-fimbria GAL3-stratified analysis, which supports uPAR and CD38 even though it does not support dPP4.

distractor_analysis.A: The conclusion (yes) is correct in direction but the reasoning is wrong. Between-region elevation of all six markers does not establish within-population co-variation with GAL3; the within-fimbria stratification is what tests that, and it specifically fails for dPP4. This is the 'cross-baseline arithmetic' failure mode.
distractor_analysis.B: The conclusion (no) is too strong. The evidence does support co-upregulation of uPAR and CD38 with GAL3 within the fimbria; the absence of dPP4 co-upregulation does not negate the uPAR/CD38 finding. The reasoning correctly identifies the relevant test but overgeneralizes the negative dPP4 result to all senescence markers.
distractor_analysis.C: The conclusion (no) is wrong because the within-fimbria GAL3 stratification does support uPAR and CD38 co-upregulation independently of the size observation. The reasoning incorrectly treats the morphological difference as the only thing the data show, ignoring the marker co-regulation evidence.

Insight3.summary: GeoMx digital spatial profiling of aged female mouse brains found that established senescence- and DAM-associated genes (Fth1, Ctss, and Apoe) and candidate or emergent genes (Ccno and Sesn3) were enriched in fimbria IBA1+ microglia relative to hippocampal IBA1+ populations. Within the aged fimbria, Apoe was the most abundantly expressed transcript in IBA1+GAL3+ relative to IBA1+GAL3− microglia and strongly distinguished these populations.
Insight3.how: The authors used GeoMx whole-transcriptome spatial profiling on 5-µm FFPE sagittal sections from 28-month-old female mouse brains, selecting areas with IBA1, GAL3, and SYTO83 and using GFAP for negative selection. They compared IBA1+ populations from hippocampus and fimbria and found enrichment of Fth1, Ctss, Apoe, Ccno, and Sesn3 in fimbria IBA1+ cells. They also compared IBA1+GAL3+ and IBA1+GAL3− populations within the aged fimbria, where Apoe was the most abundantly expressed gene in the GAL3+ population relative to the GAL3− population. Differential expression was analyzed with a two-sided DESeq2 Wald test, and the authors cautioned that GeoMx DSP is useful for signature discovery but limited for molecularly phenotyping rare or heterogeneous cell populations.
Insight3.relevant: We next examined microglial transcriptional signatures specific to the hippocampus and fimbria of old female mice using GeoMx DSP. We segmented the hippocampus and fimbria regions with positive selection based on GAL3, IBA1 and SYTO83 labels and negative selection by GFAP (Fig. 3a). First, we compared IBA1+ populations in the hippocampus versus fimbria (Fig. 3b). Established senescence and DAM genes Fth1, Ctss and Apoe and candidate senescence-related genes, Ccno and Sesn3, were enriched in IBA1+ cells of the fimbria. We next compared transcriptional profiles of IBA1+GAL3+ and IBA1+GAL3− microglia specifically in aged fimbria (Fig. 3c,d). Apoe was the most abundantly expressed gene in IBA1+GAL3+ cells, relative to IBA1+GAL3− cells. We discovered conserved senescence- and DAM-associated genes (Fth1, Apoe and Ctss) and emergent genes (Ccno and Sesn3) were enriched in aged fimbria microglia. Apoe strongly distinguished GAL3+ versus GAL3− microglia in the fimbria. These experiments underscore the utility of GeoMx for expression signature discovery; however, GeoMx DSP remains limited for molecularly phenotyping rare or heterogenous cell populations.

mcq_questions.question: GeoMx whole-transcriptome spatial profiling was performed on 5-µm FFPE sagittal sections from 28-month-old female mouse brains. Hippocampal and fimbria regions were segmented with positive selection for GAL3, IBA1 and SYTO83 and negative selection for GFAP. Comparing IBA1+ populations between hippocampus and fimbria, five genes — Fth1, Ctss, Apoe, Ccno and Sesn3 — were enriched in fimbria IBA1+ cells. Which option best characterizes what these five genes collectively indicate about fimbria IBA1+ microglia?

options.B: They indicate a generic microglial activation state because Ccno and Sesn3 are canonical activation markers in mouse microglia. because all five genes were detected only in the fimbria IBA1+ population and were absent in hippocampal IBA1+ cells.
options.C: They indicate that fimbria IBA1+ microglia adopt a senescence- and DAM-associated profile enriched in the fimbria. because Fth1, Ctss and Apoe are established senescence/DAM genes and Ccno and Sesn3 are candidate/emergent senescence-related genes that were jointly enriched in fimbria versus hippocampal IBA1+ cells.
options.A: They indicate a senescence- and DAM-associated profile that is spatially enriched in fimbria IBA1+ cells. because the enrichment combines established senescence/DAM genes (Fth1, Ctss, Apoe) with candidate senescence-related genes (Ccno, Sesn3), and the comparison was made between fimbria and hippocampal IBA1+ populations in the same brains.
options.D: They indicate that fimbria IBA1+ microglia are molecularly distinct but phenotypically undefined. because the spatial comparison identifies enriched transcripts but does not quantify protein-level changes or functional readouts of senescence.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The conclusion ('a senescence- and DAM-associated profile that is spatially enriched in fimbria IBA1+ cells') is supported because the enrichment combines (1) established senescence/DAM genes (Fth1, Ctss, Apoe) with (2) candidate senescence-related genes (Ccno, Sesn3), and (3) the comparison was made regionally between fimbria and hippocampal IBA1+ populations in aged female mouse brains. The reasoning correctly integrates the gene categories with the spatial design.

distractor_analysis.B: Fails on the conclusion: Ccno and Sesn3 are described in the source as candidate/emergent senescence-related genes, not as canonical microglial activation markers. The reasoning is also inaccurate — the genes were enriched in fimbria IBA1+ relative to hippocampal IBA1+, not detected exclusively with absence in hippocampus.
distractor_analysis.C: The conclusion ('adopt a senescence- and DAM-associated profile') is close, but the reasoning is weaker because it does not make the spatial 'enriched in the fimbria' statement explicit; it merely restates gene categories. The key is C because it explicitly ties the enrichment to the regional comparison.
distractor_analysis.D: The conclusion is too agnostic. The stated enrichment of named senescence/DAM and candidate senescence genes is itself a phenotype-level statement; saying 'phenotypically undefined' contradicts the clear transcriptomic signature described.

mcq_questions.question: In the same GeoMx DSP analysis, IBA1+GAL3+ and IBA1+GAL3− microglia were compared within the aged fimbria. Apoe was the most abundantly expressed transcript in IBA1+GAL3+ relative to IBA1+GAL3− microglia and strongly distinguished these two populations. If GAL3 were used as the sole positive-selection marker (with GFAP-based negative selection) and Apoe were excluded from the differential expression readout, which option correctly states what could and could not be concluded about the IBA1+GAL3+ population?

options.A: The senescence/DAM enrichment of fimbria IBA1+ microglia could still be assessed through Ccno and Sesn3. because these two candidate senescence-related genes were among the five enriched in fimbria IBA1+ cells in the regional comparison, so they would still register as enriched without Apoe.
options.C: The strong distinction between IBA1+GAL3+ and IBA1+GAL3− fimbria microglia would be retained. because Ccno and Sesn3 were also enriched in fimbria IBA1+ cells and therefore would substitute for Apoe in separating the GAL3+ and GAL3− subpopulations.
options.B: The senescence/DAM enrichment in fimbria versus hippocampal IBA1+ microglia could still be detected, but the GAL3+ versus GAL3− distinction within the fimbria could not be made. because Fth1, Ctss, Ccno and Sesn3 were enriched in the regional comparison, but only Apoe was reported as the most abundant transcript that distinguished IBA1+GAL3+ from IBA1+GAL3− cells in the fimbria.
options.D: Neither the regional enrichment nor the GAL3+/GAL3− distinction could be assessed. because GeoMx DSP without Apoe readout cannot detect senescence- or DAM-associated transcripts in fimbria microglia.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The conclusion is that regional enrichment remains detectable while the within-fimbria GAL3+/GAL3− distinction cannot be made. The reasoning correctly separates two distinct comparisons: (1) the fimbria vs hippocampus IBA1+ comparison, where Fth1, Ctss, Ccno and Sesn3 were enriched alongside Apoe, so removing Apoe still leaves four enriched genes; and (2) the IBA1+GAL3+ vs IBA1+GAL3− comparison within the fimbria, where only Apoe was explicitly reported as the most abundant transcript that strongly distinguished the two subpopulations, so no other gene in the list was singled out for that within-fimbria split.

distractor_analysis.A: The first half of the conclusion is correct, but the option omits the second required claim — that the within-fimbria GAL3+/GAL3− distinction depends on Apoe and would be lost. It answers only part of what the question asks.
distractor_analysis.C: Fails on the conclusion. Insight7.summary: The authors converted a recognized technical artifact of spatial transcriptomics — low-level 'molecular shadow' transcripts misassigned from neighboring cells — into an analytical asset they termed molecular 'contact-tracing.' They showed that white matter-localized microglia carry spillover oligodendrocyte/myelin transcripts (Mbp, Mobp, Plp1) while gray matter-localized microglia carry neuronal spillover (Camk2a, Adcy1, Sncb, Snap25), with astrocytic markers partitioning as Aldoc (gray) versus Gfap (white); they formalized this into canonical cell-type gene-set modules that independently corroborated their anatomical cluster assignments.
Insight7.how: The authors first performed two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum differential expression between white matter- and gray matter-localized microglia (Fig. 4e), revealing region-specific enrichment of non-microglial markers interpreted as spillover from adjacent cells. They then constructed 'contact-tracing' gene-set modules for major brain cell types from published datasets (Supplementary Table 2) and scored each CosMx microglial cluster (Fig. 4j,k; Fig. 5j; Supplementary Fig. 5). In the young-versus-old dataset, clusters 2, 3, 9, 10 and 15 scored high on the oligodendrocyte module and localized to white matter; clusters 4, 7 and 14 scored high on the neuronal module and localized to gray matter; cluster 15 additionally scored on an ependymocyte module; cluster 1 scored on the microglial/homeostatic module; and cluster 13 showed enrichment for both the homeostatic and DAM modules, consistent with a transitional state. The same logic applied to non-microglial immune cells showed aged cells carrying elevated Gfap, Plp1, Mbp, Mobp and complement transcripts relative to young cells, interpreted as proximity to resident glia. The approach was confirmed with anatomical registration.
Insight7.relevant: "An inherent artifact of current single-cell spatial platforms and segmentation algorithms is low-level detection of transcripts from adjacent or interacting cells. By exploiting this signal as a variant of molecular 'contact-tracing', we observed that white matter-localized microglia were enriched for oligodendrocyte transcripts Mbp, Mobp and Plp1, whereas gray matter-localized microglia were distinctly enriched for neuronal transcripts Camk2a, Adcy1, Sncb and Snap25, indicating close proximity to, or potentially prior engulfment of these cells (Fig. 4e). Distinct astrocytic markers were enriched in gray (for example, Aldoc) and white (for example, Gfap) matter-localized microglia (Fig. 4e)." "To profile transcripts from neighboring and/or interacting cells, we devised canonical gene set modules of distinct brain cell types (Supplementary Table 2) using previously published data and interrogated the 'contact-tracing modules' and enrichment for SenBrain and DAM signatures in clusters (Fig. 4j–k). We detected enrichment for immune cell and choroid plexus related gene modules in cluster 1, 7 and 9, oligodendrocyte module in clusters 1 and 4, neuronal module in cluster 3 and astrocyte and vascular modules in cluster 9 (Fig. 4k)." "Microglial clusters 2, 3, 9, 10 and 15 exhibited higher oligodendrocyte module scores, whereas clusters 4, 7 and 14 exhibited higher neuron module scores, corroborating the white and gray matter-majority anatomical localizations (Fig. 5j, Extended Data Fig. 4c–i and Supplementary Fig. 5a). Clusters 1 and 13 were enriched for the microglia cell-type module, suggestive of homeostatic populations, whereas clusters 3, 10 and 13 were enriched for the DAM module… Cluster 15 was enriched for an ependymocyte module, suggesting proximity to ventricular borders (Fig. 5j and Supplementary Fig. 5d)." "Relative to young immune cells, higher levels of astrocyte (Gfap), oligodendrocyte (Plp1, Mbp and Mobp), and microglia (C1qa, C1qb and Ctss) markers were detected in old immune cells, suggesting proximity to brain-resident glia (Supplementary Fig. 3d)." "Current spatial mapping molecular markers and segmentation algorithms are imperfect, resulting in detection of 'molecular shadows', corresponding to low-level transcript localizations of cell identity markers that probably originate from adjacent cells rather than the segmented cell. We exploited this methodological artifact as a way of classifying spatial neighborhood characteristics of cell populations, which were confirmed with anatomical registration."

mcq_questions.question: In a CosMx spatial transcriptomics dataset of microglia, two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum testing between white matter-localized and gray matter-localized microglia shows white matter microglia enriched for Mbp, Mobp, and Plp1, while gray matter microglia are enriched for Camk2a, Adcy1, Sncb, and Snap25. What does this pattern most directly indicate?

options.B: Microglia transcribe neuronal genes when in gray matter and myelin genes when in white matter, because regional cues drive lineage-inappropriate transcription in microglia.
options.A: Microglia in each region carry low-level transcripts from the dominant neighboring cell type, because imperfect segmentation assigns a fraction of transcripts from adjacent oligodendrocytes (white matter) or neurons (gray matter) to the microglia segment.
options.C: The differences reflect contamination of the microglial cluster by oligodendrocytes and neurons, because the gene sets are too specific to represent spillover and instead indicate misclassification of cell identity.
options.D: These transcripts are bona fide markers of microglial subtypes specialized for myelin or synaptic interaction, because the regional specificity rules out a technical artifact.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The keyed option (A) combines two premises: (1) the observed enrichment is region-matched to the dominant neighboring cell type (oligodendrocyte/myelin transcripts in white matter microglia; neuronal transcripts in gray matter microglia), and (2) this matching is consistent with low-level spillover ('molecular shadows') from imperfect segmentation of adjacent cells rather than de novo microglial transcription. The authors exploit this artifact as 'contact-tracing' evidence of proximity, not as evidence of microglial gene expression.

distractor_analysis.B: Fails on the conclusion. The matching of transcript identity to the neighboring non-microglial cell type, combined with the authors' interpretation of low-level spillover, does not support lineage-inappropriate transcription in microglia. This is a single-premise reading that ignores the artifact-based interpretation.
distractor_analysis.C: Fails on the reasoning. The authors explicitly treat the signal as low-level spillover from adjacent cells (corroborated by independent contact-tracing modules and anatomical registration), not as misclassification that would invalidate the microglial cluster identity. This misreads the evidence as a classification error rather than an exploitable proximity signal.
distractor_analysis.D: Fails on both conclusion and reasoning. The region-specific enrichment matches non-microglial canonical markers (myelin vs. neuronal genes), which is the hallmark of spillover rather than of microglial subtype identity. Treating these as bona fide microglial markers contradicts the stated evidence that the signal originates from adjacent cells.

mcq_questions.question: A separate analysis compares CosMx-defined young versus old immune cells (including microglia) for non-immune markers. Old immune cells show elevated Gfap (astrocyte), Plp1/Mbp/Mobp (oligodendrocyte), and C1qa/C1qb/Ctss (microglia) transcripts relative to young immune cells. If the 'molecular shadow' interpretation is correct, what follow-up prediction is most strongly licensed by these data?

options.A: Old immune cells upregulate astrocyte, oligodendrocyte, and complement genes intrinsically, because aging induces transcription of non-immune programs in immune cells.
options.B: The elevated glial markers in old immune cells reflect increased physical proximity of immune cells to resident glia with age, because the same spillover logic that explains region-matched transcripts predicts that any shift toward glia-rich neighborhoods produces matching marker enrichment.
options.C: The complement transcripts C1qa/C1qb/Ctss must originate from contaminating microglia, because complement genes are microglia-specific and cannot be part of an immune-cell signature.
options.D: Aging eliminates astrocyte and oligodendrocyte identity, because their canonical markers appear outside the glial lineage in immune cells.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Option B chains two premises: (1) the 'molecular shadow' mechanism assigns low-level transcripts from neighboring cells to a segmented cell, and (2) the elevated glial markers in old immune cells match the canonical markers of brain-resident glia. Combining these, the prediction that old immune cells sit closer to glia than young immune cells is directly licensed. The authors explicitly state this conclusion: 'suggesting proximity to brain-resident glia.'

distractor_analysis.A: Fails on the reasoning. The same spillover logic that produces region-matched enrichment (myelin in white-matter microglia, neuronal in gray-matter microglia) shows that non-immune markers in immune cells reflect neighborhood, not intrinsic transcription. This option asserts the opposite mechanism on the basis of a single premise (the elevation) without accounting for the established artifact.
distractor_analysis.C: Fails on both conclusion and reasoning. The immune-cell category in this comparison includes microglia themselves, and the contact-tracing framework explicitly allows microglia-derived transcripts (e.g., C1qa/C1qb/Ctss) to appear in immune-cell segments. Treating complement transcripts as impossible in immune cells contradicts the stated evidence and the framework.
distractor_analysis.D: Fails on both conclusion and reasoning. The data show elevated glial markers in immune-cell segments, which under the spillover framework indicates proximity, not loss of glial identity. Astrocyte and oligodendrocyte identity is not erased by the presence of their transcripts in adjacent immune-cell segments.

Insight8.summary: Monocle3 trajectory inference on the combined young-plus-old CosMx dataset suggests that the age-exclusive senescent-DAM population (cluster 10) can be reached by at least two anatomically distinct routes — a longer homeostatic gray-matter trajectory (1 → 13 → 3 → 10) and a more direct white-matter/ependymocyte–oligodendrocyte trajectory (8 → 15 → 3 → 10) — supporting the interpretation that microenvironmental priming, rather than a unique cellular origin, confers the convergent age-selective transcriptional signature.
Insight8.how: The authors first identified gradient increases in senescence/DAM marker expression and cell-percentage enrichment across clusters 1 → 13 → 3 → 10 (Fig. 6e). They applied Monocle3 to the integrated young+old CosMx microglia, excluding peripheral clusters unreachable from the core partition (Fig. 6f). A forward model rooted at homeostatic cluster 1 branched from cluster 3 into 9, 10, or 15 → 8 (Fig. 6g(i)); a retrograde model rooted at cluster 10 showed three precursor branches converging on it via cluster 15/8, cluster 9, and cluster 13 → 1 (Fig. 6g(ii)). The 8 → 15 → 3 → 10 route required the fewest branch points. Pseudotime distance from cluster 10 inversely correlated with SenBrain and DAM module scores. The authors interpret these convergent trajectories — alongside three non-exclusive biological scenarios — as evidence that anatomical microenvironmental context, rather than a singular lineage, shapes the common senescent-DAM transcriptional endpoint, while noting that spatially resolved lineage mapping is needed to validate these inferences.
Insight8.relevant: We next modeled fate trajectories that may give rise to age-increased microglial populations within the aged (n = 4) versus young (n = 4) dataset (Figs. 5 and 6). We examined SenBrain gene expression gradients that may indicate a trajectory from homeostatic microglia (cluster 1) toward the age-exclusive cluster 10 (Fig. 6e). Across clusters 1, 13, 3 and 10, we observed gradient increases in the percentage of cells and average expression for several senescence and DAM-associated markers, including Apoe, Axl, C4bi, Cd9, Clec7a, Ctsb, Lgals3 and Tyrobp. We applied Monocle3 trajectory inference, excluding peripheral clusters (2, 6, 11 and 12, as defined by the UMAP) that were unreachable from the main core partition (Fig. 6f). Our initial model included homeostatic cluster 1 as the pseudotime root and proceeded to cluster 13, following to 3, which then branched into 9, 10 or 15 → 8 terminal populations (Fig. 6g(i)). This 1 → 13 → 3 → 10 trajectory tracked with the age-increased transcript gradients described above (Fig. 6e) and was characterized by proportional decreases in young cell abundance (Fig. 5e(ii)). To explore alternative trajectories resulting in the age-increased populations, we interrogated a retrograde model with terminal cluster 10 as the pseudotime root (Fig. 6g(ii)). Inferred retrograde trajectories branched from cluster 10 to 3, bearing both DAM and SenBrain-enriched genes, then branched toward three trajectories: (1) ependymocyte-, astrocyte- and oligodendrocyte-associated cluster 15 and astrocyte-associated cluster 8, (2) choroid plexus and oligodendrocyte-associated cluster 9 and (3) DAM- and homeostatic-microglia-associated cluster 13 with continued branching toward neuron-associated populations, including homeostatic cluster 1 (Fig. 6g(ii)). Based on trajectory branching of subpopulations, we determined that the retrograde-inferred astrocyte-, ependymocyte- and oligodendrocyte-associated microglial trajectory involving population 15 (8 → 15 → 3 → 10) was the most direct route to cluster 10 and involved the fewest branch points, whereas the gray matter-enriched homeostatic microglial trajectory (1 → 13 → 3 → 10) contained more branch points (Fig. 6g(ii)). Pseudotime values were inversely correlated with SenBrain and DAM module scores, and the greatest pseudotime distance from cluster 10 was represented in terminal gray matter populations (Supplementary Fig. 6). The models suggest that senescent DAM cells may emerge along multiple possible molecular trajectories, probably resultant of anatomically defined microenvironment priming that ultimately confers common age-selective transcriptional signatures. Additional spatially resolved lineage mapping and cell–cell communication analyses are needed to validate lineage inferences and the context-dependent signaling networks that drive cell fate trajectories in brain aging and disease.

mcq_questions.question: In a combined young-and-old spatially resolved microglia dataset, Monocle3 was applied to a restricted partition (clusters 1, 3, 8, 9, 10, 13, 15). A forward-trajectory model rooted at homeostatic cluster 1 passes through 13, then 3, where it splits into branches terminating at 9, 10, or 15→8. A retrograde model rooted at the age-exclusive cluster 10 branches backward to 3, then splits toward (a) 15→8, (b) 9, and (c) 13→1. Through the 8→15→3→10 route, cluster 10 is reached with fewer branch points than through the 1→13→3→10 route. Which interpretation is best supported by these observations?

options.A: Cluster 10 is produced by a single lineage because both the forward and retrograde models converge on a unique route with the fewest branch points.
options.C: Cluster 10 lies at the convergence of at least two anatomically distinct trajectories (a longer homeostatic gray-matter path 1→13→3→10 and a more direct white-matter/ependymocyte–oligodendrocyte path 8→15→3→10) because the retrograde model reveals three separate precursor branches feeding into it.
options.B: Cluster 10 must originate from white-matter ependymocytes because the shortest pseudotime path passes through ependymocyte-associated clusters.
options.D: Cluster 10 is the unique root of microglial aging because the retrograde model places it at the pseudotime root and pseudotime inversely correlates with SenBrain/DAM scores.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The keyed option combines two premises: (i) the retrograde model rooted at cluster 10 splits into three branches — through 15→8, through 9, and through 13→1 — demonstrating multiple precursor routes, and (ii) one of these (8→15→3→10, ependymocyte/oligodendrocyte-associated) is more direct than another (1→13→3→10, homeostatic gray-matter). Together these premises support the interpretation that cluster 10 is reachable by at least two anatomically distinct trajectories of differing lengths.

distractor_analysis.A: The conclusion is wrong: the forward model itself shows three forward branches from cluster 3 (toward 9, 10, and 15→8), and the retrograde model shows three precursor branches, so the evidence supports multiple, not single, routes. The reasoning collapses two separate routes into one.
distractor_analysis.B: The reasoning is correct that the 8→15→3→10 path is shortest, but the conclusion overreaches: 'must originate' is not licensed because a shorter pseudotime route is not a necessity test and the trajectories are computationally inferred, not validated.
distractor_analysis.D: The reasoning mixes two premises (retrograde rooting and pseudotime–module correlation) but the conclusion is wrong: pseudotime was rooted at cluster 10 only in the retrograde model, and an inverse correlation between pseudotime and SenBrain/DAM scores means cells farther from cluster 10 score lower on these modules, which is consistent with cluster 10 being a terminal age-selective state rather than a unique origin.

mcq_questions.question: Given that Monocle3 trajectory inference on the integrated young+old microglia partition returned (i) a forward-rooted graph in which cluster 3 branches into terminal clusters 9, 10, and 15→8, (ii) a retrograde graph in which cluster 10 has three precursor branches (15→8, 9, 13→1), and (iii) the 8→15→3→10 route reaching cluster 10 in fewer branch points than 1→13→3→10, while pseudotime distance from cluster 10 inversely correlates with SenBrain/DAM module scores and clusters 1, 13, 3, 10 show gradient increases in senescence/DAM markers (Apoe, Axl, C4b, Cd9, Clec7a, Ctsb, Lgals3, Tyrobp) — which conclusion is licensed by the stated evidence about how cluster 10 arises?

options.A: Cluster 10 arises from a unique precursor lineage, because the most parsimonious pseudotime path identifies 8→15→3 as the obligatory origin route.
options.D: Anatomically distinct microenvironments can produce the same transcriptional endpoint, because at least two divergent routes (8→15→3→10 and 1→13→3→10) terminate at cluster 10 alongside the shared 3→10 segment.
options.B: Cluster 10 cannot be age-exclusive because multiple branches feed into it from young-cell-enriched clusters.
options.C: Cluster 10 is unnecessary for the age-increased transcriptional signature, because pseudotime inverse correlation with module scores shows other clusters carry higher DAM/SenBrain expression.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Chain three premises: (1) forward branches from cluster 3 and three retrograde precursor branches from cluster 10 indicate multiple incoming routes; (2) one route involves white-matter/ependymocyte/oligodendrocyte-associated clusters 8 and 15, while the other involves homeostatic gray-matter clusters 1 and 13 — i.e., two anatomically distinct contexts; (3) the shared 3→10 segment shows that despite different upstreams, the same transcriptional endpoint (cluster 10, with its age-enriched senescence/DAM signature) is reached. Combined, these support a microenvironmental-priming interpretation in which distinct anatomical routes converge on a common age-selective endpoint.

distractor_analysis.A: The reasoning ('fewest branch points = obligatory origin') is invalid: parsimony in a trajectory graph is not a necessity test, and the forward model shows cluster 10 as one of three terminal branches from cluster 3, not a unique one.
